- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.1) and price is trending upward, model often overreacts; cap forecast increase at 1.5% above recent 7-day average.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is negative and price is trending downward; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% per day from day 5 onward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment values), model often fails to adjust for mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward bias for 3–5 days after the spike.
